# An exact obstruction to the entire fixed-weight unequal-endpoint selector

This disproves the universal claim that the selector body Y from
`candidate 0acdf1c3867a889d` always contains an OC
point under the nonheavy-volume conditions. It does NOT refute OC. It also
does not refute an algorithm that checks optimal points in the endpoint
fibers in addition to Y, or one that allows a different centroid weight.

## 1. A genuine five-dimensional convex body

Let B be the standard four-dimensional simplex in R^4, with volume V.
Its first centroid coordinate is 1/5. Put

    alpha=17/100, beta=199999/1000000,
    L=B intersect {alpha<=x_1<=beta},
    m=|L|/V=(83/100)^4-(800001/1000000)^4,
    q=m^(-1/4), A=(2-q)L, C=qL.

The exact rational comparisons are

    m-1/16=2481161996159996799999/10^24>0,
    (101/200)^4-m=56588628840003200001/10^24>0.

Consequently 200/101<q<2. The two endpoint fibers are positive bodies.
Their relative volumes are

    |C|/V=1, |A|/V=a=(2m^(1/4)-1)^4, 0<a<10^(-8).

Convexity of L gives the exact Minkowski identity (A+C)/2=L subset B.
Thus the convex hull of the lifted fibers A,B,C at -1,0,1 is a full convex
body in R x R^4 with exactly those three integer fibers. At the two extreme
indices the fibers are exact. At zero every convex combination is a mixture
of B and (A+C)/2, so it contributes nothing beyond B. Its mixed volume is
(2+a)V. Each of its three fiber volumes is strictly less than half that
total: 1<(2+a)/2 and a<(2+a)/2.

## 2. Every point in Y belongs to one bad cap

For ANY measure sigma<=1_C dx of mass |A|=aV, the selector is

    y=[V g_B+aV g_A+integral x d sigma]/[V(1+2a)].

All points of A have first coordinate at least (2-q)alpha, and all points
of C have first coordinate at least q alpha. This applies equally to the
ordinary centroid of A and to the mean of any such fractional selector.
Therefore every y in the ENTIRE selector body Y satisfies

    y_1>=h=(1/5+2a alpha)/(1+2a)
           =1/5-3a/[50(1+2a)].

In particular h>beta, since 1/5-beta=10^(-6), whereas
3a/[50(1+2a)]<6*10^(-10).

Consider the single closed ambient halfspace

    H={x_1+(1-q)beta z>=h}.

On the fiber at -1 its maximum affine margin before subtracting h is
(2-q)beta-(1-q)beta=beta. On the fiber at +1 it is
q beta+(1-q)beta=beta. Both endpoint fibers are therefore entirely excluded.
Every point (0,y) with y in Y belongs to H.

The retained fraction of the middle simplex is

    |B intersect H_0|/V=(1-h)^4
       =gamma_4[1+3a/(40(1+2a))]^4,
    gamma_4=(4/5)^4.

For 0<a<=1, the elementary mean-value bound gives

    [1+3a/(40(1+2a))]^4-1
       <=[1+3a/40]^4-1
       <=(3a/10)(43/40)^3
        =(238521/640000)a < a/2.

Hence

    vol_MI(S intersect H)<gamma_4(1+a/2)V
                         =(gamma_4/2)vol_MI(S).

This is a strict, exact, all-selector upper certificate. It covers arbitrary
fractional densities sigma, not merely uniform subsets or selected cap
centroids. The algebraic coefficients q,a are exactly defined positive
real numbers; rationality is not an assumption of the proposed selector
principle or of OC.

## 3. Scope of the obstruction

The conditional theorem with equal endpoint volumes is unchanged. The
failed proposal fixes the center as the centroid of 1_B dx+2eta while
discarding the unselected part of an unequal endpoint. Allowing a free
mixture weight changes the candidate family and is not refuted here.

Nor is nonheavy volume equivalent to failure of an endpoint center. The
ordinary maximum depth of a nonsimplex endpoint can exceed gamma_4. An
endpoint point already meeting OC would resolve this example regardless
of Y. No claim that the endpoints fail the OC target is made in this note.
